declaredBy: [A8 §9 item 4]'s plan §8.3(1) — the symptom index's authored half
note: The ONE hand-written input to tools/generate-symptom-index.ts. Everything else in the generated symptom index — the reference concepts' existence, their retention state, their owed state — is derived from src/, data/ and catalog/index.json. This file holds only what cannot be derived: which legacy MoveManager module corresponds to which reference concept. The reference model is built from external sources only ([SD §0]) and knows nothing about MoveManager, so EVERY correspondence here is [ORIGINAL] — our judgment, not a source's. That is why each row carries its own `basis`: what in the legacy code the reading was taken from.
purpose: A session refactoring legacy WinForms logic arrives holding a MODULE FOLDER or a FORM NAME, never a fact class. glossary.md is indexed by vocabulary (Aggregates, Record types, Bases) and offers no path in from a symptom. This table is that path.

legacySource.note: Counts below were MEASURED at that commit, not estimated: .vb files excluding .Designer.vb, walked per module folder. They are captured here because the generator runs in CI, where movemanager does not exist. They WILL drift — they are context for ranking, not a contract, and `measuredAt` is how a reader knows how stale they are.

elsewhere.note: Not in the module folders, and relevant to how much migration is left.

confidenceLegend.read: The correspondence was taken from form names AND at least one form or folder listing was opened this session.
confidenceLegend.fromNames: Taken from form names alone. The names in this domain are unusually literal, but a form named for a noun can still hold logic about three others.
confidenceLegend.unknown: Could not be named without reading the code. Recorded as unknown rather than guessed — [SD §0]'s disclosure rule applies to this table too.

modules.basis: SaleMaintenanceForm, SaleMemosMaintenanceForm; the only module folder carrying a ViewModel already.
modules.note: "Sale" is the legacy word for the booked job, which the reference splits into an `order` (the commitment) and a `shipment` (the goods). [A1] and the order↔shipment cardinality fork are the reading; do not assume one legacy Sale row is one of either.

modules.basis: InvoiceMasterMaintenanceForm, BudgetMasterMaintenanceForm — the second-largest module at 8,872 lines.
modules.note: `charge` exists but its VALUE is owed (A7/A12 — the corpus publishes gross/net/discount as field names and defines them nowhere), and `chargeCollection` is an ABSENT fact class. So this module's biggest concepts are the ones the reference is thinnest on. Read [A7] before trusting a mapping here.

`driver` IS a published role name. Settlement is compensation — A13's revenue allocation, which [A8 §5 row 11] explicitly must not be read as settling ([A8 §9 item 7]). Driver settlement logic is therefore OUT of the reference's scope, not merely owed.

Employees and commissions are an INTERNAL HR/payroll axis. The reference models parties as ASSERTERS of facts, not as employees, and has no commission concept. Mostly out of scope — but `partyRole` and [A8 §3]'s role⟂ownership separation are the right reading for who-may-do-what.

Accessorials. Crating is a packing service, so `packing` is the act; the money is `charge` at `aspect = PROPOSED/DECIDED/RATED`. The THIRD-PARTY half is delegation-shaped and lands on [A8 §9 item 4], which is OPEN — so who may assert a third party's service is undecided.

THE ROUND THAT CHANGED THIS ROW IS THE ONE TO READ. Until catalog 0.8.0 this module mapped to NOTHING: survey, estimate and cube were all absent fact classes, and the index said so rather than leaving a migrator with silence. [A10] (2026-10-12) minted survey and estimate, so the two largest concepts here now have authority rows (19 and 20) and a named asserter, the contractingCarrier. What is still missing is cube — the surveyed VOLUME. The survey act is published and one of the values it produces is not, which is a narrower gap than this row used to describe: cube needs a MeasureValue in a volume unit and unitOfMeasure is still owed. Read [A8 §5] rows 19-20 before mapping a save button here, and note that estimate's VALUE shape is owed to A7/A12 even though the fact class exists.

One of the best-covered modules: A5 is written, `stay` is an aggregate, and the storeIn/storeOut acts are distinguished from the `sitEntryDate` VALUE ([SD §5.3] — a date is not an instant, and the two must not be substituted). But `stayAuthorisation`, `stayTermination` and `stayAllowance` are ABSENT fact classes, so the lifecycle edges are owed.

COMMERCIAL warehousing, and the reference's corpus is household-goods. "Project" has no reference concept at all. Treat A5's readings as analogies here, not as mappings — and note `Pegasus.Domain` already has its own `CommercialWarehouse` context, which may be the better target.

Pre-commitment. [A7 §3.6] and [A1] establish that both roles ARE named before any commitment exists — §375.401's estimate signed by both parties before the BOL, and §375.409's broker-adopted estimate — so a lead is not nothing to the reference. But there is no `lead` or `opportunity` concept, and `estimate` is absent. `src:sirva-ade`'s LEP/LEU/LOD specs are the closest published material. UPDATED at catalog 0.8.0: estimate and survey were listed here as ABSENT fact classes until [A10] minted them. A lead that carries an estimate now has somewhere to go — and the asserter is the contractingCarrier, not the booker, because §375.409 makes even a broker-authored estimate the carrier's own.

"Account" is the commercial counterparty. The reference's nearest role is `accountParty` — A8-NAME-2's half of the word "shipper": the party that contracts and pays, as distinct from `goodsOwner`, the party whose goods move. That distinction is load-bearing and was the catalog's first BREAKING change (`customer` → `goodsOwner`, 0.7.0); do not collapse the two.

[A8 §9 item 3] decided that crew-member grain rides on the ROLE and the identifying scheme, never on a class field on the party. "Crew history" is the effective-dated role assignment A8-HISTORY needs, so this module is probably the best legacy evidence for it.

[SD §8.4] is the directly relevant decision: a day of service performed at one place with no linehaul IS a Trip with one Stop. That is what makes a local job expressible at all, and it was added because the model could not previously hold one.

`resource` is the aggregate. [SD §1.2]'s `resource` row is UNCITED for half of what it admits — "driver or crew member" carries no citation (recorded by [A8 §9 item 3]) — so the vehicle/driver split inside `resource` is weaker than it looks. Repair/maintenance has no reference concept.

A REPORTING shape — "flash" is a period recap across accounting, billing, claims and customer service. The reference publishes ASSERTIONS and holds that state is a projection ([SD §1.1] forbids a mutable current-state field), so a flash report is downstream of the model and has no fact class by construction. Its `claim` form is the exception and points at an ABSENT class. Do not look for a `flash` concept; there will never be one.

Rate tables for automobile transport. Lands on `charge` at `aspect = RATED`, whose authority is "the tariff owner — the van line, or the party whose tariff prices it" — and that holder is STILL OWED to [A8 §9 item 2], blocked on `secondary` grade, carried as `{kind: 'owedRole'}`. So the reference can say this is a rating fact but cannot say who owns the rate.

Internal workflow. The nearest reference concept is `notification`, whose fact-class FAMILY is itself owed, and [A8 §9 item 6] — the party as a notification target — is open. An internal task list is probably not a domain fact at all.

modules.basis: TextingApplicationHost, ToastUnreadTextNotifier — only 89 lines here; the real SMS code is in Pegasus.SMS_Library.
modules.note: Channel mechanics, not domain. [SD §6.5]/[A8 §9 item 6]: an obligation knows WHOM it is owed to but cannot say HOW they are reached — so the reference deliberately stops short of channels. Nearly all of this module is out of scope.

READ [A8 §9 item 3] BEFORE TOUCHING THIS. It decided there is NO `person` aggregate kind and no person/organisation field on the asserter: a party's grain rides on the role and on the identifying scheme. `tests/conformance/party-grain-refuses.ts` refuses the `person` spelling outright. A legacy Person table is not evidence against that; it is the thing the decision was taken about.
Customer-facing document access. [A6] and [A8 §5 row 17] cover document ISSUANCE — the issuer of the document's own number scheme, and nobody else. Portal access control is not a domain fact.
Reference/master data maintenance across several domains. It has no single correspondence — map FORM BY FORM, using the other rows. Its settlement forms are A13's, like `_Driver`'s.
Operational monitoring of the application itself. Not domain.

modules.basis: FormSupport, PostalAddressMaintenanceForm — the LARGEST module at 10,014 lines across 38 forms.
modules.note: Shared UI plumbing, and the largest module by line count, so expect to meet it constantly. Mostly not domain — BUT its address handling touches the one thing [SD §1.2] admits it lacks: there is NO `place` aggregate, and `placeRef` is owed (carried as `{owed: 'placeRef'}` in `custody.ts`'s `LegEndpoint`). An address is the clearest example of a legacy concept the reference deliberately does not model yet.
Application configuration. Not domain.
Infrastructure. Not domain.
Infrastructure. Not domain.
Menu/report wiring. Not domain.
Test and scratch forms. Not domain, and note some are not obviously test-only despite the folder name.

The name says unsorted and it is: 25 forms with no single theme. Its two largest ARE dispatch, so [A3]/[A4] apply there, but map this folder FORM BY FORM. The highest-value module to triage, because it is large and nobody has classified it.
